title: Draft: xml: Use libxml2 only to parse DTD configuration files
description:
Use libxml2 to parse the DTD configuration files and remove the flex-based parser.

Still register the protocols and media types immediately (as they're needed for handoffs) and continue to delay the field registration, because of its performance impact.

Ping #20508

notes.body: @mmann78 this is based on your draft MR for the parsing. I think this is where I'd like to end up. Profiling shows that this has minimal impact on startup by not doing the last layer of recursive parsing and field registration. (Doing that at startup makes packet-xml take longer than any other protocol to register.)

Is the need for wmem_ptr_array really hurting the startup performance? I keep wanting to not delay the field registration at startup for simpler logic, hoping we can just "fix" the performance.  I see a lot of copying, so is the complexity then become ownership of the memory of "XML data strings" from the DTDs?

Yeah, I definitely understand. Some of it is the copying. The `fully_qualified_name` calls actually contribute a fair amount - those seem like the easiest target to optimize, probably by instead of reconstructing the full name each time, starting with the immediate parent's name and adding the last ".%s" onto that. The `duplicate_element` names are also a lot too, but I haven't looked into those as much.

There's some small savings that might add up that I see in various places. For example, there's ptr arrays created of elements and attributes, which are then turned into maps (why not maps directly?). When turning the arrays into maps, `g_ptr_array_remove_index()` is used instead of the `_fast` version (but we don't care about the order since it's being put in a map, so we might as well use the _fast version or even better start from the end, which is always fast.)
If we allocate some of the strings in epan scope originally, then we can probably steal some of the strings from dtd_data instead of wmem_strdup'ing them yet again.

I agree that, unlike some other protocols, the total number of fields registered doesn't look *that* high here (there some startup overhead just from registering fields and putting them in the big map).
!20721 helps a bit.

I started down the path of using wmem_list instead of GPtrArray because an array is never needed, everything thing is iterated and never indexed.  My current state is that I probably have "memory leaks", but all in the wmem_epan_scope().  Working off of the tweaks from this MR that bugfixed my draft.

I also confirmed that this produces the same fields for all the DTDs, including the more complicated `smil.dtd` (that has several Elements in a row, then several AttrLists, and also has parameter entities to substitute.)

This gets into the question I originally asked about libxml2 datatypes versus glib (and when to switch over)

Yeah. Apparently the Windows debug build, something in how the strings are allocated, it will complain about memory segmentation if you `g_free` an `xmlChar*` that libxml2 allocated. Other OSes don't complain. I ended up switching over earlier because I have a goal of eventually allocating these strings in wmem_epan_scope, and then reducing the cleanup at shutdown.

This, along with some wmem_map changes I made recently, are another reason why it would be nice to have a wmem_ptr_array. You can somewhat fake it with wmem_array, but there's a lot of useful APIs and syntactic sugar in g_ptr_array.

commits_data.title: xml: Use the libxml2 parsed data to register fields
commits_data.message:
xml: Use the libxml2 parsed data to register fields

Remove the flex-based parsing. Store the dtd_build_data_t produced
on startup by the libxml2 parsing (which registered the protocol
names and media type handoffs, which are necessary for other dissectors)
and then use it when needed to build the hierarchy of fields.

Do this because make_xml_hier is still fairly slow with all the memory
allocation, recursive processing, and field registration.

Ping #20508
